headline: CHINA RARE EARTH EXPORT PAUSE EXPIRES TODAY — USAR AND MP MATERIALS BRACE FOR WHAT COMES NEXT
snippet: China's two-month rare earth export waiver pause expires on November 10, leaving Western buyers without certainty on future supply availability. USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) and MP Materials are the primary domestic beneficiaries — both have been highlighted as the key US producers positioned to fill the gap if China restricts exports further or declines to extend the pause.

headline: BUNKER HILL AND SILVER47 CLOSE MERGER — "MADE IN AMERICA" SILVER PRODUCER BORN WITH FOUR U.S. PROJECTS
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining and Silver47 Exploration completed their merger on November 6, 2026, creating a U.S.-focused silver and critical minerals producer. Through the acquisition Silver47 added silver-rich projects in Alaska, Nevada and New Mexico to Bunker Hill's Idaho asset; Silver47 shares are set to delist from TSX-V, Frankfurt and OTCQX around November 9.

headline: USA RARE EARTH Q3: $3M REVENUE, $1.2B CASH — FIRST HEAVY RARE EARTH SALES IN OCTOBER FROM BRAZIL
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) reported Q3 2026 revenue of $3 million, below expectations due to supply constraints, but beat EPS estimates at a loss of $0.02/share vs. $0.13 expected. The company ended the quarter with $1.2 billion cash and confirmed its first heavy rare earth mixed carbonate (MREC) deliveries from Serra Verde, Brazil began in October — the first Western-hemisphere heavy rare earth commercial sales in years.

headline: COPPER SNAPS WORST WEEKLY SLIDE SINCE MARCH — LME PRICE $13,939/T AS CHINA YANGSHAN PREMIUM HITS RECORD $230
snippet: LME three-month copper held around $13,939 per tonne on Monday after shedding 2.7% last week in its steepest decline since March, as physical tightness in China reasserted support. The Yangshan copper premium surged to a record $230 per tonne, signalling genuine import demand even as Citi cut its three-month copper forecast to $13,300 from $14,500.

headline: GOLD SLIDES $64 TO $4,075 TODAY — CPI DATA TRIGGERS POSITION UNWIND AS DOLLAR FIRMS
snippet: Gold dropped $64.20 to $4,075.20 per troy ounce on November 10 as U.S. CPI data firmed the dollar and triggered profit-taking across precious metals. The pullback follows a sustained run above $4,100 and comes amid debate over whether gold is consolidating before another leg higher or setting up a correction toward $3,500 as some analysts have flagged.

headline: DYNASTY METALS FINDS NEW GOLD ZONE IN PELHAM FOOTWALL — UNEXPECTED DISCOVERY EXPANDS ONTARIO SYSTEM
snippet: TSXV-listed Dynasty Gold (TSXV: DYG) reported a new gold discovery in the footwall of its Pelham deposit in Ontario, an unexpected find that extends the mineralized system beyond the previously defined envelope. Footwall discoveries at established deposits are high-value exploration hits — they can materially grow resources without requiring greenfield permitting.

headline: GOLDSTORM HITS 407m OF GOLD-SILVER EQUIVALENT AT CROWN NEXT TO KSM — SURPRISE SILVER-RICH INTERCEPT
snippet: Goldstorm Metals drilled its Crown project — adjacent to Seabridge Gold's giant KSM deposit in BC's Golden Triangle — for the first time and hit 407.55 metres of 0.39 g/t gold equivalent in hole OR-26-03, with the intercept heavily weighted toward silver rather than gold. The scale and precious metals tenor at a KSM-adjacent project is a meaningful exploration signal in one of North America's premier mining districts.

headline: LOTUS RESOURCES SHIPS FIRST URANIUM CONCENTRATE FROM MALAWI — KAYELEKERA RESTART DELIVERS
snippet: Lotus Resources has shipped its first uranium ore concentrate from the Kayelekera mine in Malawi, a milestone that marks the successful restart of a project mothballed since 2014. Kayelekera is one of the few non-Kazakh, non-Cameco uranium operations outside the established Athabasca Basin producers to reach production in the current uranium cycle.

headline: KAZAKH PRESIDENT ORDERS 100-YEAR URANIUM STRATEGIC RESERVE — AIMS TO SECURE OWN REACTOR FUEL SUPPLY
snippet: Kazakhstan's president directed the government to build a strategic uranium reserve sufficient to supply the country's planned nuclear power plants for more than 100 years. As the world's largest uranium producer (~43% of global output), Kazakhstan stockpiling for domestic use adds a new long-term constraint to global uranium supply that Western utilities are only beginning to price in.

headline: PARAGUAY PRESIDENT PEÑA RESIGNS — POLITICAL CRISIS CLOUDS URANIUM ENERGY'S SOUTH AMERICAN PLANS
snippet: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña submitted his resignation amid a banking crisis and ongoing impeachment proceedings — weeks after Uranium Energy Corp announced exploration plans in the country. Political instability in a jurisdiction where the company had staked an early-mover position adds permitting risk and timeline uncertainty to those assets.

headline: ERAMET PUTS LITHIUM AND NICKEL ASSETS UP FOR SALE TO SLASH DEBT — CENTENARIO PLANT NOW AT FULL PRODUCTION
snippet: French mining major Eramet is seeking buyers for stakes in its lithium and nickel operations to reduce its debt load, even as its Centenario lithium plant in Argentina reached full production last month. The forced asset sales signal that even large diversified miners are struggling with the low lithium price environment, potentially creating acquisition opportunities for well-capitalized buyers.

headline: GOLD MINERS VALUATION GAP AT DECADE WIDE — 5.7x EV/EBITDA VS. MARKET: VALUE TRAP OR BUYING OPPORTUNITY?
snippet: Discovery Alert's November analysis quantifies the gold miner valuation gap at approximately 5.7x forward EV/EBITDA — well below the broader market multiple and near decade lows — and asks whether persistent discounts reflect structural undervaluation or a rational market verdict on operating risk. The piece frames stagflation-driven gold demand against rising cost pressures that have already forced guidance cuts at Ivanhoe and other majors.

headline: SURGE BATTERY METALS REBRANDS AS LITHIUM X2 MINING — TRADES AS LIXX ON TSX-V FROM NOVEMBER 9
snippet: Surge Battery Metals completed its corporate rebrand to Lithium X2 Mining, effective November 9, and now trades under the ticker LIXX on the TSX Venture Exchange. The rebranding signals a narrowed strategic focus on lithium exploration from a previously broader battery metals mandate — a common restructuring move as management tries to capture investor attention in a commodity-specific story.
